limitations.statement: No counterexample was sought against the underlying claim about nontrivial Collatz cycles: doing so would require exhibiting an actual nontrivial cycle, which is computationally infeasible and open-problem-adjacent. The computational checks covered numeric and boundary structure only: the convergents p13, p15 and p16, both Farey identities, and the three boundary inequalities.

limitations.short: No counterexample was sought against the underlying nontrivial-cycle claim; that is infeasible

limitations.statement: The independent check (Gate 9) ran patched copies of both external tools: lean4export and nanoda with a faster decimal conversion/parse of large number literals, because this proof contains literals of up to 25.6 million digits. The patches touch text conversion only, not type-checking, and were tested (identical export prefix, five earlier passes reproduce, a corrupted literal is rejected). The patched builds exist only on the recording machine; the two diffs are published beside the run.
limitations.short: The independent check used patched copies of lean4export and nanoda (huge-literal handling)
